extracted.intended_audience: graduate students / advanced undergraduates in algebraic geometry and homological algebra
extracted.subtask_description: Exposition and working rules for double complexes, spectral sequences (construction, pages, differentials, convergence, and sample applications) followed by the motivating definition and basic properties of sheaves (restriction maps, germs/stalks).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filtered colimits commute with homology (ModA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Show that filtered colimits commute with homology in ModA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is stated as Exercise 1.6.L; hint: use the FHHF Theorem (Exercise 1.6.H) and the previous exercise. Think about how limits and colimits commute with homology in general and which way maps go.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exactness of inverse limits with surjective transitions
rubrics_metrics.description: If ... → An → An−1 → ... is an inverse system of exact sequences of modules with the transition maps An+1 → An surjective (transition maps of the left term are surjective), then the limit 0 → lim An → lim Bn → lim Cn → 0 is exact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 1.6.M: you must define the maps in the limit sequence and use surjectivity of the left-term transitions. This principle will be used later (Chapter 29).

rubrics_metrics.name: Left-exact functors suggest derived functors / long exact sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: When you see a left-exact functor F and an exact sequence 0 → M' → M → M'' → 0, the left-exactness of F yields 0 → FM' → FM → FM'' → ... and one should 'dream' that this continues into a long exact sequence; these continuation terms are the derived functors R^i F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is conceptual guidance: in good cases a natural continuation exists and is useful (see Chapter 23). The remark applies to left-exact and contravariant functors as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition / structure of a double complex
rubrics_metrics.description: A double complex is a collection of A-modules E_{p,q} (p,q ∈ Z) with horizontal maps d: E_{p,q} → E_{p+1,q} and vertical maps d: E_{p,q} → E_{p,q+1} satisfying d^2 = 0 for each direction and either all squares commute or all anticommute (you may switch by signs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conventions: first superscript = column (x-coordinate), second = row (y-coordinate). You may assume squares anticommute; sign changes convert commuting to anticommute. Variations (vertical arrows downwards, some E_{p,q}=0) are straightforward. Visual diagrams are helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total (single) complex associated to a double complex
rubrics_metrics.description: The total complex E^• has E^k = ⊕_i E_{i,k−i} (the kth anti-diagonal sum) with differential d = d_horizontal + d_vertical (with signs as needed), and d^2 = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The cohomology of this total complex is called the hypercohomology of the double complex; often just 'cohomology of the double complex'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approximate definition of a spectral sequence (pages, differentials, orientation)
rubrics_metrics.description: A spectral sequence (rightward orientation) is a sequence of tables/pages E_{p,q}^r (r = 0,1,2,...) with differentials d^r : E_{p,q}^r → E_{p−r+1,q+r}^r satisfying d^r ∘ d^r = 0 and E^{r+1} is the cohomology of E^r with respect to d^r.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Orientation indicates which differential is the 0th differential (here rightward). Each E_{p,q}^r is a subquotient of E_{p,q}^i for i<r. Visual order of morphisms (d0,d1,d2,...) helps. If E_{p,q}=0 then all E_{p,q}^r = 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of first pages: E^0, E^1, E^2
rubrics_metrics.description: E^0 is the table of entries of the total complex viewed as rows/columns; d^0 is horizontal differential so E^1 is the table of row cohomologies; on E^1 there are induced vertical maps making columns into complexes, and E^2 is the cohomology of E^1 with respect to those.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You should check induced vertical maps on row cohomologies. The connecting homomorphism construction for d^2 is reminiscent of the Snake Lemma / long exact sequence arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convergence / abutment of a spectral sequence and filtration on H^k(total)
rubrics_metrics.description: For first quadrant (or appropriately bounded) double complexes the spectral sequence stabilizes: for fixed p,q the modules E_{p,q}^r stabilize as r→∞ to E_{p,q}^∞, and there is a filtration of H^k(E^•) by subobjects whose successive quotients are the E_{p,k−p}^∞ (displayed in (1.7.2.2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Terminology: say the spectral sequence 'converges to' or 'abuts to' H^•(E^•). Tip: later-page differentials point deeper into the filtration; arrowhead direction indicates subobjects vs quotients.

rubrics_metrics.name: When spectral sequences determine H^• (collapse / easy cases)
rubrics_metrics.description: If all E_{i,k−i} are zero except maybe one, or if E^r has just one nonzero row/column (i.e., spectral sequence 'collapses' at stage r), then H^k(E^•) can often be determined exactly; over a field one can at least compute dimensions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In lucky circumstances E^2 (or a small page) may already equal E^∞. Use these collapse criteria to compute cohomology in examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of spectral sequences to prove standard exactness lemmas
rubrics_metrics.description: Spectral sequences can be used as a bookkeeping device to prove results such as the Snake Lemma, the Five Lemma (and subtler variants), the mapping cone long exact sequence, and that a short exact sequence of complexes yields a long exact sequence in cohomology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises 1.7.5–1.7.F illustrate these uses: plug diagrams into the spectral sequence with appropriate orientation to read off exactness. Practicing these examples builds confidence with the machinery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal goals for defining/verifying spectral sequences (1.7.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Precisely: (a) describe E_{p,q}^r (b) verify H^k(E^•) is filtered by E_{p,k−p}^∞ (c) describe d^r and verify (d^r)^2=0, and (d) verify E_{p,q}^∞ is the cohomology computed using d^r.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the checklist items to complete a rigorous construction and proof of the spectral sequence formalism (the section 1.7.7/1.7.9 addresses this).

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete strip-based construction of pages and differentials (p,q)-strips and r-closedness
rubrics_metrics.description: Define a (p,q)-strip as an element whose nonzero entries lie on an upper-leftwards semi-infinite antidiagonal starting at (p,q); Sp,q^r = set of r-closed (p,q)-strips (stable under r), define X_{p,q}^r and Y_{p,q}^r from these and set E_{p,q}^r = X_{p,q}^r / Y_{p,q}^r. The differential d^r is induced by the total differential mapping Sp,q^r to Sp−r+1,q+r^r.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises 1.7.H–1.7.J guide verification (stabilization, kernel/image calculations) and show d^r ∘ d^r = 0 and that cohomology of d^r is E^{r+1}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheaf axioms (motivating example: sheaf of differentiable functions)
rubrics_metrics.description: A sheaf of functions assigns to every open U a ring O(U) with restriction maps res_{V,U}: O(U) → O(V) for V ⊂ U; these satisfy compatibility (restricting in two steps equals direct restriction), locality (if sections agree on an open cover they are equal), and gluing (compatible local sections on a cover glue to a global section).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The differentiable (or continuous, smooth, plain) functions example illustrates these three key properties. This is the intuitive motivation before the formal definition of presheaf/sheaf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Germs and stalks; stalks as colimits and local rings
rubrics_metrics.description: The germ at p is the equivalence class of (f,U) where f is defined near p; the stalk O_p consists of these germs and is the colimit of O(U) over neighborhoods of p. The ideal m_p of germs vanishing at p is maximal, making O_p a local ring with O_p / m_p ≅ R (value at the point).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises: show m_p is the only maximal ideal (every element not in m_p is invertible). Interpret value at a point via quotient by m_p. Note mp/m_p^2 relates to cotangent space in smooth manifold case.
